subject: Post-call: Nimbus POC parity probes, decision criteria & next tests
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@nimbus.ai>, Priya Raman <priya.raman@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Nimbus POC parity probes, decision criteria & next tests

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the time today — appreciate the candid run-through of current infra and the evaluation timetable. Quick recap while it's fresh and proposed next steps so nothing gets lost: 

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Latency spikes during concurrent batch jobs (peak 50–100ms over SLA during payroll runs)
- Cost variability across model sizes + burst workloads (need more predictable unit economics)
- Data isolation and audit log retention for regulatory review (SOC2 scope)

Primary goals for the POC:
1) Demonstrate consistent 95th percentile latency below 120ms for your 1k qps baseline
2) Show a cost envelope for sustained 1k qps and for burst to 2k qps
3) Prove auditability (per-request logs, retention policy export) and a secure key management path

Decision criteria you gave weight to:
- Latency/SLO compliance (40%)
- Cost per 1k tokens under baseline (30%)
- Security/compliance fit (20%)
- Ease of ops / integration (10%)

Open questions we captured on the call:
- Which competitor models do you want parity tested against? (you mentioned "current provider + internal trimmed model + Vertex")
- Your exact token mix distribution for the payroll run (short prompts vs long responses) — Priya to share the sample traces
- Any nonfunctional test windows when we should avoid traffic (regulatory blackout windows)

Proposed POC test plan (high level):
- Week 0: exchange test traces and access (you provide sample traces + allow our sandbox access)
- Week 1: smoke tests (latency baselines, model variant sanity)
- Week 2: parity runs (our best-ops config vs named competitors, per-token cost calc)
- Week 3: production-like soak and audit log export validation

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Priya: share token mix and sample traces (by Tue 07/21)
- Alex: confirm competitor list for parity (you said CurrentProvider and Vertex — please confirm)
- Camila: deliver parity test plan + initial scripts (I attached v1) by Tue 07/21
- Jordan: provision sandbox credentials and schedule live window (I will send invite)

Attachments: nimbus-parity-test-plan-v1.xlsx, redwood-competitive-matrix.pdf (call recording attached as stub)

If that matches what you captured, agree and we'll lock the kickoff for Wednesday next week.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Blake | Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jordan — good summary. Confirming a few points from our side: 

1) Competitors to include for parity: CurrentProvider (we'll provide API endpoint), Vertex (GCP hosted model), and our internal trimmed model (v0.9).
2) Priya will send token mix and three representative request traces by EOD Tuesday.
3) For SOC2 items: please include details on retention windows, whether logs can be exported in NDJSON, and an outline of KMS/HSM options. We'll need that for our Security team.

Procurement looped in to expedite the NDA + SOW once we have the test plan. Pricing bands are something we'll review after the parity runs — happy to get rough T-shirt numbers in advance.

Alex

Jordan — quick internal follow-up based on Alex's confirmation. I mapped the parity matrix and the concrete tests we'll run: 

Parity candidates (explicit): CurrentProvider (v-prod), Vertex (text-generation-3), Nimbus-internal (v0.9)
Test suite (short):
- Latency ramp: sustained 1k qps with 10% burst to 2k qps; measure p50/p95/p99 over 1h window
- Request-size sensitivity: run with your token mix (short/med/long) to capture cost delta
- KV-cache effect: enable prefix cache vs disabled to measure token/cost savings
- Audit export: simulate export of 30 days of logs, verify NDJSON schema and retention export time
- Failure modes: simulate node OOM and verify graceful fallback to smaller model variant

We should also include a small head-to-head prompt quality check (10 curated prompts) so Nimbus can sanity-check output parity — this helps them trust cost comparisons.

I'll attach the test-plan v1 to the thread (already in Jordan's attachment list). I propose we schedule our first live window on Wed 07/22 09:00–11:00 PT — Jordan, can you provision creds and invite?

Camila
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
